reason: I'll start the rhythmic pump by adding muscle to the heart chambers so they can produce a pumping force.
expectation: The chambers will gain pumping walls, though they may still need valves and a rhythm.

alternatives.reason: I considered assembling the blood first, but chose to start with the pump.

effect: The chambers now have muscular walls to push blood, so I can add direction control next.
reaction: The distinction between containing blood and producing pressure makes sense.
reason: I'll add the valves to help control the direction of blood flow through the pump.
expectation: The valves will fit into the chambers and help prevent blood from flowing backward; the pump may still need a rhythm.

alternatives.reason: I considered assembling the blood, but chose to continue building the pump.

effect: The valves provide direction control, so the remaining pump task appears to be establishing a rhythm.
reaction: The explanation that valves respond to pressure makes their role clear.
reason: I'll add the pacemaker cells to give the muscular pump a rhythm.
expectation: The pacemaker cells will help coordinate rhythmic contractions of the heart chambers.

alternatives.reason: I considered assembling blood next, but want to finish the pump first.

effect: The heart now beats on its own rhythm, completing the pump goal. Next I need to build the filled returning circuit.
reaction: It was interesting that the heart starts its own rhythm without a separate brain order for each beat.
reason: I'll combine plasma and red blood cells to make the blood that will fill the circuit.
expectation: I expect to create blood for the circulation, though the vessels will still need to be connected.

alternatives.reason: I considered connecting the vessels first, but chose to make the circuit's contents.

effect: The blood is assembled, so the remaining visible step is to connect parts of the vessel network.
reaction: The distinction between plasma as the fluid and red blood cells as oxygen carriers is clear.
reason: I'll combine the arteries and capillary networks; it's the only offered combination and should advance the circuit.
expectation: I expect a connected vessel route, though veins and the heart may still need to be added.

effect: The arteries and capillaries form an outward route with a place for exchange; veins appear to be the next part of the returning circuit.
reaction: The explanation of why capillaries are needed makes the route more meaningful.
reason: I'll add the veins to complete the return route; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the veins to connect the exchange vessels back toward the heart, though the blood and pump may still need to be joined to the circuit.

effect: The vessels now form a returning circuit, so the next step is to fill it with blood.
reaction: Closing the route back to the heart makes the circuit easier to picture.
reason: I'll add the oxygen-carrying blood to the vessel circuit; it is the only offered combination and advances the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect a filled vessel circuit, which may still need to be connected to the beating heart.

effect: The vessel circuit is filled, and the new goal is to connect it to the pump.
reaction: Putting the blood into the returning route makes the separate parts feel ready to work together.
reason: I'll connect the beating heart to the filled circuit; it's the only offered combination and matches the new goal.
expectation: I expect a working circulation in which the heart moves blood through the vessels and back, though the model may have further goals.

effect: The heart and filled vessel circuit now form a circulation, completing the chapter and showing how flow continually brings blood to distant tissues.
reaction: Connecting the pump and route was satisfying because their separate roles came together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the vessel route was most worthwhile, especially learning that capillaries allow exchange with tissues and veins provide a return path. Those details connect circulation to the cells' need for supplies.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filling the circuit felt fairly predictable after making the blood and vessels, although it helped assemble the model.

surprise.text: I was interested that cells in the heart start its rhythm without a separate brain command for every beat.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the later combinations offered only one choice at a time and required little decision-making.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue to see how circulation connects to supplying the working arm. The explanations made the parts' different jobs clear, though I would hope for more meaningful choices.
